title: Ops Atelier: Action Aggregator for composable runbooks-as-tasks
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Oncall and support engineers repeatedly assemble short, ad-hoc runbooks from disparate admin utilities (SSH helpers, cert rotators, DB rollbacks, cache clears). Resulting playbooks are brittle, hard-to-review, and often executed as uni-directional scripts with limited telemetry or dry-run capability.

Goal: Build an Action Aggregator service (Ops Atelier) that turns small admin utilities into composable, versioned runbook tasks ("playlets") that can be: (a) composed into multi-step runbooks, (b) executed in dry-run mode, (c) replayed safely with idempotency checks, and (d) gated by RBAC and approval flows. The service should prioritize safety, observability, and low-latency interactive use for first-line support.

Scope: 
- Define a lightweight task schema for playlets (inputs, outputs, safety hints, undo metadata).
- Implement an "intent normalizer" that maps human intent (short form) to a concrete playlet plus parameters.
- Build an aggregator microservice that composes playlets into runbooks and produces an executable task graph for the runbook-runner.
- Add dry-run, replay, and undo token primitives.
- Integrate RBAC checks and approval hooks with the console's policy engine.
- Emit structured telemetry (token-level cost, execution latency, outcome, undo success rate) to the Console dashboards for per-playlet visibility.
design_notes:
We prefer a small, opinionated schema rather than a generic DSL. Playlet metadata will include: id, semantic-category, preconditions, undo_hint, estimated_tokens, side_effect_tags. The aggregator will not execute primitives itself; it emits a typed task graph consumed by the runbook-runner runtime. Security: each playlet will declare required permissions; the aggregator validates access via a policy call before returning an executable graph.

Trade-offs considered:
- Synchronous composition (low latency for interactive flow) vs. async compilation (better for long graphs). Initial MVP will be synchronous for <8-step paths and fall back to async for larger ones.
- Rich DSL vs. typed playlets: typed playlets are easier to review and to tie telemetry to; we chose typed playlets for safety and production observability.

Open decisions: naming for undo tokens, approval UX (in-console vs. Slack), and whether to allow arbitrary shelllet execution in playlets (currently disallowed).
implementation_plan:
Milestone 1 (week 1): schema + spec + conformance tests. Milestone 2 (week 2-3): aggregator service (compose API) + intent normalizer prototype + unit tests. Milestone 3 (week 4): dry-run mode, idempotency tokens, and RBAC integration. Milestone 4 (week 5): integrate with runbook-runner, add telemetry, and public console surface.

Engineering tasks: API design, catalog format, CLI shim for developers, schema validator, aggregator service, connector for console approval flow, runbook-runner adapter, e2e QA harness.

Acceptance criteria:
- Playlet schema published and reviewed.
- Aggregator API can compose and return a deterministic task graph for at least 10 canonical playlets.
- Dry-run returns a validation report without executing side effects.
- RBAC enforcement prevents unauthorized execution in tests.
- End-to-end demo: support engineer composes a 3-step runbook and executes with dry-run, approval, and live run; telemetry appears in Console.
rollout_plan: Phased rollout: internal alpha for SRE and core support (opt-in) -> broader support team beta (two weeks) -> GA behind feature flag with audit logging turned on by default. Provide a migration tool to convert frequently used ad-hoc scripts into playlets. Early-bird customers (internal) will be asked to contribute 5 high-value playlets to seed the catalog.
telemetry: Emit per-playlet metrics: executions.total, executions.success, executions.fail, dryrun.count, undo.invoked, mean_latency_ms. Tag metrics with playlet_id, team, and release. Add tracing spans for aggregator.compose, policy.check, runbook-runner.exec. Create a Console dashboard with top failing playlets and median dry-run validation time.
risks:
- If approval hooks are slow, interactive flows break; mitigate with async approvals and optimistic dry-run caching.
- Incorrect undo hints could create dangerous remediation paths; mitigate by requiring an SRE sign-off for playlets that modify critical resources.
- RBAC integration depends on policy service availability; include a fallback deny-mode and circuit-breaker with clear error messages.
